# spec/contract/chars

`spec/contract/chars` — the character-level checks a contract's text needs:
UTF-8 decoding one code point at a time, control characters, and the
patterns its ids, sections and numbers are written in. Each pattern is a
plain scan rather than a regex, so what it admits is read off the code.

Generated from [src/spec/contract/chars.ts](https://github.com/amritk/vector/blob/main/src/spec/contract/chars.ts).

## Declarations

### charsCodePointAt

The code point that starts at byte `i` of `s`, read as UTF-8. A malformed or
overlong sequence, a surrogate, or one past U+10FFFF reads as U+FFFD.

```ts
function charsCodePointAt(s: string, i: i32): i32
```

<scalar-field name="s" type="string" required>

the text

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="i" type="i32" required>

a byte index in `s`, below `s.length`

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

the code point

</scalar-field>

### charsSequenceLength

How many bytes the UTF-8 sequence at byte `i` takes: 1 for ASCII and for a
byte that cannot start a well-formed sequence, so a scan always advances.

```ts
function charsSequenceLength(s: string, i: i32): i32
```

<scalar-field name="s" type="string" required>

the text

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="i" type="i32" required>

a byte index in `s`, below `s.length`

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

1 to 4

</scalar-field>

### charsFromCodePoint

The UTF-8 text of one code point, so code can name an invisible or
confusable character by its number rather than spell it in the source.

```ts
function charsFromCodePoint(cp: i32): string
```

<scalar-field name="cp" type="i32" required>

a code point, at most U+10FFFF

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

its UTF-8 encoding, one to four bytes

</scalar-field>

### charsName

A code point as `U+XXXX`: uppercase hex, at least four digits.

```ts
function charsName(cp: i32): string
```

<scalar-field name="cp" type="i32" required>

the code point

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

the code point's name, such as `U+000A` or `U+1D400`

</scalar-field>

### charsIsControl

Whether a code point is a control character: C0, DEL, C1, or the Unicode
line and paragraph separators, any of which would end a line in a comment.

```ts
function charsIsControl(cp: i32): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="cp" type="i32" required>

the code point

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

true for a control character

</scalar-field>

### charsFirstControl

The first control character in `s`, by name.

```ts
function charsFirstControl(s: string): string | null
```

<scalar-field name="s" type="string" required>

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string | null">

</scalar-field>

### charsIsStringText

Whether every byte of `s` is printable ASCII, tab, LF or CR: the characters
a contract's strings may be written with, each one byte.

```ts
function charsIsStringText(s: string): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="s" type="string" required>

the text

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

true when `s` uses only those characters

</scalar-field>

### charsIsLowerHex

Whether `s` is lowercase hex: an even number of digits, or exactly `digits`
of them when `digits` is not negative.

```ts
function charsIsLowerHex(s: string, digits: i32): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="s" type="string" required>

the text

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="digits" type="i32" required>

the number of digits wanted, or -1 for any even number

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

true when `s` is lowercase hex of that length

</scalar-field>

### charsTestVector

The number a test case's name gives it: `Test Vector #N`, exactly, with N
a positive number written without a leading zero.

```ts
function charsTestVector(s: string): i32
```

<scalar-field name="s" type="string" required>

the name

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

N, or 0 when `s` is not such a name

</scalar-field>

### charsIsSection

Whether `s` is a section number: digits in dot-separated parts (`2.3`), or

```ts
function charsIsSection(s: string): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="s" type="string" required>

the text

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

</scalar-field>

### charsIsAbs

Whether `s` is a non-negative decimal in RFC 8259 §6 number syntax, as a

```ts

```

<scalar-field name="s" type="string" required>

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

</scalar-field>

### charsIsF64Text

Whether `s` is an f64's text: a decimal in RFC 8259 §6 number syntax, or


<scalar-field name="s" type="string" required>

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

</scalar-field>
